interest: This file provides valuable insight into the administrative recordkeeping and intelligence monitoring of the U.S. State Department regarding Japanese naval exercises during the interwar period. Although the file bundle consists of List of Papers docket sheets rather than the full despatches, the purports capture critical strategic assessments, notably Japanese doctrine for utilizing the South Seas Mandate (Caroline and Marshall Islands) to stage continuous air and naval attrition attacks against the U.S. Navy if it advanced toward the Philippines in the event of war. Furthermore, the records highlight Foreign Minister Shidehara's defense rhetoric in the Diet following the London Naval Conference, the staging of joint Army-Navy propaganda maneuvers in August 1933, and regional diplomatic surveillance of Japanese fleet movements coordinated across Tokyo, Paris, and Batavia.
overview: This file (894.31 Japan, Naval Maneuvers, File 534) consists of Department of State List of Papers docket sheets indexing records and communications on Japanese naval maneuvers between 1930 and 1936. The entries record diplomatic despatches, military intelligence, and cross-reference sheets tracking Japanese naval exercises, beginning with an announcement and press analysis of Japanese Navy air corps maneuvers in the Caroline and Marshall Islands in June 1930, including Japanese operational assumptions regarding continuous attrition against the U.S. Pacific Fleet. Subsequent entries index reports by Ambassador Joseph C. Grew on joint Army-Navy propaganda maneuvers conducted in August 1933, a report forwarded via the Navy Department citing Paris press coverage of Japanese naval maneuvers in 1935, and reports on fleet maneuvers forwarded by Consul Walter A. Foote from Batavia in May 1936. Together, these sheets document American diplomatic and naval surveillance of Japan's expanding maritime operations and post-London Naval Conference defense policies.

subfiles.about: A Department of State List of Papers docket sheet indexing communications on Japanese naval maneuvers from 1930 to 1933.
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet (Form DS-46) indexes records under decimal file 894.31 concerning Japanese naval maneuvers between 1930 and 1933. Entry No. 9 lists Despatch No. 160 from Edwin L. Neville in Tokyo reporting on scheduled Japanese Navy air corps maneuvers in the Caroline and Marshall Islands, citing a Jiji Shimpo article and analyzing Japanese defense strategy against the U.S. fleet en route to the Philippines, alongside Foreign Minister Shidehara's statements to the Diet on defense capabilities post-London Naval Conference. Entry No. 11 cross-references Despatch No. 510 from Joseph C. Grew (filed under 894.00 P.R./69) reporting on joint propaganda maneuvers staged by the Japanese Army and Navy in August 1933.
subfiles.title: Department of State List of Papers: Naval maneuvers--Japan (Entries 9 and 11)

subfiles.about: A Department of State continuation List of Papers docket sheet indexing documents and cross-references on Japanese naval maneuvers from 1935 to 1936.
subfiles.summary: This continuation sheet (designated Page #3) of the List of Papers for decimal file 894.31 logs communications regarding Japanese naval maneuvers. Entry No. 12 records a Navy Department memorandum citing the U.S. Naval Attaché in Paris quoting an article from the French newspaper Le Temps on Japanese naval maneuvers. Entry No. 13 cross-references Despatch No. 433 from Walter A. Foote in Batavia (filed under 756d.94/11) forwarding reports regarding maneuvers of the Japanese fleet.
subfiles.title: Department of State List of Papers: Naval Maneuvers - Japan (Entries 12 and 13)
